question.value: Investigate the interstellar chemistry of cyanides (CN) and isocyanates (NCO) and the reservoir of interstellar prebiotic molecules via the C2H3NO isomers CH3NCO and HOCH2CN towards Serpens SMM1-a and IRAS 16293B.

evidence.quote: These two species are investigated to study the interstellar chemistry of cyanides (CN) and isocyanates (NCO) and to gain insight into the reservoir of interstellar prebiotic molecules.
In this work, the detection and analysis of the isomers HOCH 2 CN and CH 3 NCO towards SMM1-a are presented and compared with literature results of IRAS 16293B and those of other sources.

analysis_steps.goal: Synthetic spectrum fitting and column density determination

method.value: Initial by-eye LTE synthetic spectrum fit in CASSIS using CDMS/JPL line lists, followed by MCMC chi-squared minimisation on optically thin unblended transitions to derive N_T, T_ex, V_LSR, and ΔV; scale optically thick main isotopologues from minor isotopologues.

evidence.quote: Given a spectroscopic line list as input, CASSIS can produce synthetic spectra of a molecule based on parameters such as column density ( N T ), excitation temperature ( T ex ), peak gas velocity ( V LSR ), line width at half maximum (∆ V ), and source size (θ source ).
The by-eye fit results were given as starting parameters for the MCMC χ 2 minimisation routine.
The main isotopologues of CH 3 OH and HNCO are optically thick and their column densities are therefore determined from minor isotopologues.

key_parameters.value: T_ex free range: 50 – 350 K; N_T free range: two orders of magnitude centered on by-eye fit

evidence.quote: The column density was given as a free parameter over two orders of magnitude centered on the by-eye fit column density and the excitation temperature was a free parameter
For SMM1-a, ∆ V was a free parameter from 1.0 – 4.0 km s −1, and the source velocity was a free parameter between 6.0 – 9.0 km s −1 .
The source size was assumed to be equal to the beam size and taken to be 1 ′′ . 2, resulting in a beam filling factor of 0.5.

claims.hypothesis: C2H3NO isomer abundances are governed by thermodynamic equilibrium vs. kinetic processes.
claims.experiment: Measure column densities and abundances of the isomers CH3NCO and HOCH2CN towards SMM1-a using ALMA Band 6 observations and CASSIS LTE MCMC fitting.
claims.result: CH3NCO and HOCH2CN have equal abundances within error bars in SMM1-a: N_T = (6.4±1.9)×10^14 cm^-2 ([CH3NCO]/[CH3OH] = 5.3×10^-4) and N_T = (7.4±0.9)×10^14 cm^-2 ([HOCH2CN]/[CH3OH] = 6.2×10^-4), whereas thermodynamic equilibrium favors CH3NCO by at least 10^9 at 300 K.
claims.finding: The formation of CH3NCO and HOCH2CN is driven by kinetic processes rather than thermodynamic equilibrium.

claims.hypothesis: HOCH2CN and HNCO abundances differ between the intermediate-mass protostar SMM1-a and the low-mass protostar IRAS 16293B.
claims.experiment: Compare molecular ratios relative to CH3OH, HNCO, and other species between SMM1-a and IRAS 16293B (PILS full-beam offset) using statistical distance analysis.
claims.result: HOCH2CN and HNCO are enhanced in SMM1-a compared to IRAS 16293B with statistical distances σ ranging from 3 to 6, whereas CH3CN, NH2CN, CH3CH2OH, and a-(CH2OH)2 show almost no relative variation.
claims.finding: HOCH2CN and HNCO are significantly more abundant in SMM1-a than in IRAS 16293B, likely due to thermal and energetic processing of HCN in warm (>30 K) ice mantles rather than simple radical-radical addition.

evidence.quote: Fig. 9 highlights that HOCH 2 CN and HNCO are more abundant in SMM1-a (σ ranging from 3 – 6) and CH 3 NCO is moderately more abundant in SMM1-a (σ ≥ 2).
The molecular ratios of HOCH 2 CN hint that the formation of this molecule does not heavily depend on solid-state radical-radical addition reactions, such as HOCH 2 + CN and HO + CH 2 CN.

claims.hypothesis: CH3NCO formation is chemically linked to HNCO across interstellar star-forming environments.
claims.experiment: Compare gas-phase [CH3NCO]/[HNCO] ratios in SMM1-a with literature measurements in IRAS 16293B, Orion KL, Sgr B2(N), G10.47+0.03, and G+0.693.
claims.result: [CH3NCO]/[HNCO] is uniform at ~10% (6.4×10^-2 in SMM1-a) across hot core and hot corino sources spanning four orders of magnitude in luminosity.
claims.finding: CH3NCO and HNCO are chemically linked and their ratio is set early in star formation, likely via solid-state methylation in ice mantles during the dark cloud or warm-up stage.

evidence.quote: The ratios of CH 3 NCO and HNCO are generally similar at [CH 3 NCO] / [HNCO] = ∼10% and vary only by a factor of a few, in particular when the lowest and highest ratio are omitted.
Therefore, the lack of source-to-source variation in [CH 3 NCO]/[HNCO] ratio hints that the abundances of these species are set at an early stage of star formation.

why_this_data.value: Simultaneous detections of CH3NCO and HOCH2CN in sources beyond IRAS 16293B were needed to overcome a sample size of one and constrain C2H3NO isomer chemistry.

evidence.quote: Due to this limited sample size, it is difficult to derive correlations or variations in the C 2 H 3 NO isomer chemistry and therefore simultaneous identifications in other sources are required.

limitations_admitted.value: Observational spatial scales and extraction positions differ between SMM1-a (~500 au, continuum peak) and IRAS 16293B (~70 au, full-beam offset), which may affect molecular ratio comparisons.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the chemical inventory of SMM1-a and the involved chemical processes are investigated on a much larger spatial scale of roughly 500 au, compared to about 70 au for IRAS 16293B.
Therefore, when comparing molecular ratios between the two sources, they may not only be affected by different physical conditions but also due to the way the sources were observed.

limitations_admitted.value: Baseline subtraction in IRAS 16293B is challenging due to line-richness and can be over-subtracted, causing dips at some HOCH2CN line positions; two temperature components may also be blended.

evidence.quote: We note that due to the line-richness of the source the baseline subtraction is challenging and in some cases, it can be oversubtracted.
This could indicate that two gas components are traced, as also shown by Zeng et al. (2019), but at this position these components are hard to distinguish.

limitations_admitted.value: D2CO lines in SMM1-a are blended and the D/H ratio of H2CO in SMM1-a is unknown, preventing a firm conclusion on the H2CO correlation with HOCH2CN.

evidence.quote: However, care needs to be taken with this interpretation, since the D 2 CO spectral lines in the SMM1-a spectrum are blended and thus there is a large uncertainty on its column density. At the same time, the D/H ratio of H 2 CO is not known in SMM1-a, which introduces another source of uncertainty.

referee_caveats_inferred: Assuming source size equals the 1''.2 beam size for SMM1-a may underestimate column densities if the hot corino emission is more compact than the beam.

Using the tentative/upper-limit column density of HOCH2CN at the full-beam offset position of IRAS 16293B (where compact emission is missed) may exaggerate the HOCH2CN enhancement in SMM1-a relative to IRAS 16293B.
